name: Coffee, ready-to-drink
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid coffee, as consumed at single strength (canned and bottled coffee, cold-brew and nitro coffee in sealed retail packaging, ready-to-drink coffee drinks); assessed on the liquid as sold ready to drink, the lot the applicant packages and the auditor samples
scope_note: Ready-to-drink coffee beverages: canned and bottled coffee, cold-brew and nitro coffee in sealed retail packaging, and other liquid coffee drinks sold ready to drink. This is the as-consumed liquid form of the coffee commodity and is certified in its own wet basis; the dry coffee commodity (beans, grounds, pods, instant solids) is certified separately in the as-sold dry basis on the Coffee page, and the two bases are never mixed and no brewing, extraction or reconstitution factor is invented between them. A ready-to-drink coffee carrying added milk routes to Category 24 for the dairy fraction; a coffee drink with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. Hong Kong Cap 132V writes the product-form split itself, setting Coffee beverages at 200 ug/kg lead as consumed against Coffee beans at 500 ug/kg as sold; HMTc preserves that split. Metals in a ready-to-drink coffee are those extracted into the water plus any packaging contribution, so the nearest applicable sovereign instrument for the water-borne analytes is the drinking-water quality standard, adopted by disclosed read-across on the as-consumed basis.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|bottled water|water intended|portion ordinarily consumed|\bbeverage\b
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling in the as-consumed basis. Every anchor must be written in a wet as-consumed, ready-to-drink, or drinking-water basis; the guard refuses any as-sold dry-commodity coffee cell, because applying a dry bean, ground or powder maximum level to a ready-to-drink liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.label: Lead 200 ug/kg is the direct sovereign maximum level for the ready-to-drink coffee form: Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 sets Coffee beverages at 0.2 mg/kg as consumed under its Note 11 (beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink). Hong Kong is the only sovereign that writes a coffee-beverage cell, and it sets the beverage form at 200 against the dry bean at 500; HMTc preserves that split.
Pb.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup on the exact product form and basis. Hong Kong Cap 132V is the only credible sovereign that regulates coffee beverages, and 200 ug/kg is the value it sets for the ready-to-drink form. The drinking-water lead limits (US bottled water 5, and the other packaged and public-water values) are stricter but are written for water sold as water, not for a coffee beverage; Hong Kong assessed the coffee beverage itself and set 200, and that product-specific value binds. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Cd.label: Cadmium 2 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from the Australian NHMRC drinking-water guideline (0.002 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed cadmium value for a water-based beverage. No sovereign sets a cadmium limit for coffee beverages; a ready-to-drink coffee is a water-based drink and takes the drinking-water cadmium ceiling.
Cd.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign regulates cadmium in coffee beverages. A ready-to-drink coffee is predominantly water, so the nearest applicable as-consumed instrument is the drinking-water quality standard; NHMRC's 0.002 mg/L is the strictest and binds by read-across. It is achievable: cadmium in brewed and canned coffee is characteristically well below this level. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

tAs.label: Total arsenic 10 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2020/2184 drinking water (0.010 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed arsenic value for a water-based beverage, and the enforceable parent ceiling for the inorganic-arsenic species bound.
tAs.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign sets an arsenic limit for coffee beverages; the drinking-water arsenic ceiling is the nearest applicable as-consumed instrument for a water-based beverage. EU 2020/2184's 0.010 mg/L is the strictest and binds. Serves as the parent ceiling for reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic carries no coffee-beverage-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of total arsenic bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling adjudicated for this row (iAs <= tAs = 10 ug/kg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot reaches the trigger min(species limit, 50 percent of the total-arsenic ceiling). Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.
iAs.regulatory_basis: No sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for coffee beverages; bounded by total arsenic, which this row governs by drinking-water read-across.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2020/2184; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110; NHMRC 2025; Hong Kong Cap 132V — none sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for a coffee beverage.
iAs.substantiation: Bounded by the total-arsenic cell (tAs = 10 ug/kg).

tHg.label: Total mercury 1 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2020/2184 drinking water (0.001 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed mercury value for a water-based beverage.
tHg.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign sets a mercury limit for coffee beverages; the drinking-water mercury ceiling is the nearest applicable as-consumed instrument. EU 2020/2184's 0.001 mg/L is the strictest and binds. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a water-based coffee beverage and is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), bounded by the total-mercury ceiling adjudicated for this row (1 ug/kg); no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 1 ug/kg); methylmercury speciation is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage; methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish and marine matrices. Bounded by total mercury, which this row governs by read-across.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2020/2184; US FDA; Hong Kong Cap 132V; NHMRC 2025 — none sets a methylmercury limit for a coffee beverage.
MeHg.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 1 ug/kg).

Ni.label: Nickel 20 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2020/2184 drinking water (0.020 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed nickel value for a water-based beverage.
Ni.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign sets a nickel limit for coffee beverages; the drinking-water nickel ceiling is the nearest applicable as-consumed instrument. EU 2020/2184's 0.020 mg/L binds. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Sn.source_scope: canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, except canned dried and canned powdered products
Sn.label: Tin 100000 ug/kg (100 mg/kg) is a disclosed read-across from EU 2023/915 canned beverages, the direct sovereign inorganic-tin ceiling for the packaging pathway that produces tin in this form. Tin in a ready-to-drink coffee is a can and can-lining migration pathway; a non-canned bottled coffee has no tin source and complies trivially.
Sn.substantiation: Disclosed read-across from the sovereign canned-beverage tin cell, which governs the tinplate-can form directly and is the only tin source in a ready-to-drink coffee. EU 2023/915's 100 mg/kg binds; the looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150 mg/kg) is disclosed and not adopted. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Al.label: Aluminium 200 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2020/2184 drinking water (0.200 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed aluminium value for a water-based beverage; the US bottled-water and Australian drinking-water aluminium limits converge on the same 200. The dry coffee commodity is held to the far higher dry-food aluminium ceiling (100000 ug/kg) in its own as-sold basis; the two bases are never mixed.
Al.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign sets an aluminium limit for coffee beverages; the drinking-water aluminium ceiling is the nearest applicable as-consumed instrument, and EU 2020/2184, US bottled water and NHMRC all set 200. Aluminium is a Tier-2 analyte with both an agronomic and an aluminium-can packaging pathway in this form. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Cr.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg
Cr.source_scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters
Cr.label: government read-across: Hong Kong Cap 132V total chromium 50 for bottled or packaged drinking waters, the nearest same-basis (liquid, as consumed) sovereign TOTAL-chromium ceiling for a ready-to-drink beverage. Replaces the NHMRC hexavalent-chromium drinking-water row, a species instrument that can never anchor a total-metal cell (audit C6, the brief's mandatory refute); value unchanged at 50.

Cr-VI.label: Hexavalent chromium 10 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from the US-California public-water hexavalent-chromium maximum contaminant level (0.010 mg/L), the strictest applicable as-consumed hexavalent-chromium ceiling and the binding chromium health control for this water-based beverage.
Cr-VI.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a coffee beverage; the US-California drinking-water hexavalent-chromium MCL (0.010 mg/L) is the strictest applicable as-consumed instrument and is the health-relevant chromium control. It is consistent with the total-chromium cell (Cr-VI 10 <= total Cr 50). Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.
